title: Minimum Array End
description: You are given two positive integers `n` and `x`. You must construct an array `nums` of `n` strictly increasing positive integers (`nums[0] < nums[1] < ... < nums[n - 1]`) such that the bitwise AND of all `n` elements equals `x`. Return the minimum possible value of `nums[n - 1]`.
hints: Every element of `nums` must have all set bits of `x` turned on, so the smallest possible `nums[0]` is `x` itself and only the zero-bit positions of `x` are free to vary.
The `(n - 1)`-th strictly larger valid number is formed by writing the binary bits of `n - 1` directly into the 0-bit slots of `x` from LSB to MSB.

examples.explanation: For n = 3, x = 4 (100), the minimal array is [4, 5, 6] (100, 101, 110), whose last element is 6.
For n = 2, x = 7 (111), the minimal array is [7, 15] (0111, 1111), whose last element is 15.
For n = 1, the array is just [x] = [10].
